title: How it works: animated system diagram (16:9)
description: A 24-second 16:9 concept explainer in the diagram style of maths and engineering channels: the title rises and glides into a header, four labelled nodes with code-drawn line icons appear one per beat at the tips of self-drawing arrows, packets stream along the arrows to show the flow, the current node is lit with a caption explaining it while the camera frames what exists so far, and the last beat lights the whole system with a takeaway. Code-rendered (scene.how-it-works) with a procedural lo-fi bed, a click on each node and a swell when the system lights.

copy_examples.brief: Explain how a home solar setup powers a house: solar panels on the roof turn sunlight into direct current; an inverter converts it to the alternating current the house uses; appliances use what they need first; any surplus is exported to the grid through a smart meter. Make it clear the house uses its own power before selling any.

inputs.title: How rooftop solar powers a home
inputs.caption_1: Panels turn sunlight into direct current
inputs.caption_2: The inverter turns it into the AC your home uses
inputs.caption_3: Appliances use what they need first
inputs.caption_4: Any surplus is exported through a smart meter
inputs.takeaway: Your home uses its own power before selling any

copy_examples.note: Nodes are the parts exactly as the brief names them, in the order energy flows; each caption is one fact from the brief in plain words; icons are the nearest concrete objects; the takeaway restates the brief's main point without adding numbers or claims.

style.typography: Inter, heavy title, bold node labels, medium captions

direction.action: Title into header; four nodes appear in flow order at the tips of self-drawing arrows, packets flow, the current node is lit and captioned; the whole system lights with a takeaway

notes: The animation is code (recipes/scene/how-it-works) rendered frame-exactly on a virtual clock; the content model supplies copy, four icon choices, a layout (flow or loop) and a look.
Copy is fitted with measured glyphs: all node labels share one size, all captions share one size, and the recipe throws rather than overflow (node labels max 24 characters, captions 72, takeaway 64).

At 24 s the nodes land at 2.95, 7.40, 11.85, 16.30 s (clicks), the title morph whooshes at 2.37 s and the system lights at 20.4 s (swell peaking at 20.7 s), derived from the recipe's intro, beat and outro formulas.

Node labels, captions and the takeaway are written from the brief, and a writer must report missing parts rather than invent them; nothing checks that mechanically (node names rarely appear verbatim in briefs), so a reviewer must confirm the flow is correct and in the right order (accuracy_review).

quality_gates.description: Integrated loudness lands within 1 LU of the -16 LUFS delivery target.
Decoded true peak stays at or below -0.5 dBTP after AAC encoding.
No stretch of blank picture (no visible contrast, any colour) lasts longer than 0.5 seconds.
A subject-matter reviewer confirms the parts, their order and every caption are correct, with no step invented or left out.
